products.name: Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success
products.shortDescription: A practical guide to cultivating deep, distraction-free focus.
products.longDescription: Deep Work lays out a framework for training your ability to focus without distraction on cognitively demanding tasks. Delivered as a DRM-free EPUB and PDF, readable on any device, with lifetime access to future revisions.

reviews.author: Priya N.
reviews.body: Changed how I structure my mornings. Read it twice.

reviews.author: Marcus T.
reviews.body: Dense in places but the core argument is worth it.

products.name: Clean Architecture: A Craftsman's Guide
products.shortDescription: Software structure and design principles for maintainable systems.
products.longDescription: A guide to the architectural principles behind long-lived, testable software: boundaries, dependency rules, and the trade-offs between them. Includes downloadable diagrams and companion code samples in the EPUB package.

reviews.author: Dana K.
reviews.body: Reference-quality. I keep coming back to chapter 22.

reviews.author: Owen R.
reviews.body: Some examples feel dated but the ideas hold up.

reviews.author: Yuki S.
reviews.body: Best explanation of the dependency rule I've read.

products.name: The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition
products.shortDescription: Timeless, practical advice for software craftsmanship.
products.longDescription: A fully revised edition covering topics from personal responsibility to architectural techniques, updated for modern development practices. Includes the original tips list as a quick-reference PDF insert.

reviews.author: Leah B.
reviews.body: Every developer should read this early in their career.

products.name: Atomic Habits
products.shortDescription: An easy and proven way to build good habits and break bad ones.
products.longDescription: A practical framework for improving daily habits, built around the four laws of behaviour change. Delivered as EPUB, MOBI, and PDF with an accompanying habit-tracking template.

reviews.author: Grace P.
reviews.body: Simple, actionable, and it actually stuck.

reviews.author: Tomas V.
reviews.body: Good ideas but repetitive by the last third.

products.name: PixelForge Studio — 1-Year Licence
products.shortDescription: Professional raster and vector image editing suite.
products.longDescription: A full-featured image editor for photo retouching, vector illustration, and layered compositing. This licence covers one seat for twelve months, including all point releases and priority email support.

reviews.author: Ines M.
reviews.body: Genuinely rivals the big-name editors at a third of the price.

reviews.author: Carlos D.
reviews.body: Great value; the plugin ecosystem is still growing.

products.name: TaskFlow Pro — Lifetime Licence
products.shortDescription: Project and task management for small teams.
products.longDescription: A lifetime licence for TaskFlow Pro, covering unlimited projects, Gantt views, and up to ten team seats. One-time payment, no recurring fees, includes all future major versions.

reviews.author: Wendy A.
reviews.body: Paid once two years ago, still gets free updates.

reviews.author: Sam O.
reviews.body: Solid, though the mobile app lags behind desktop.

products.name: SecureVault Password Manager — 2-Year Licence
products.shortDescription: Encrypted password and secrets manager for individuals.
products.longDescription: End-to-end encrypted vault for passwords, passkeys, and secure notes, with browser extensions for every major browser and biometric unlock on mobile. Two-year single-user licence, key delivered by email immediately after purchase.

reviews.author: Hana J.
reviews.body: Migration from my old manager took ten minutes, flawless since.

products.name: CodeSight Static Analyzer — Team Licence
products.shortDescription: Static analysis and linting for polyglot codebases.
products.longDescription: A static analysis suite covering Python, TypeScript, and Go, with CI integration and a shared dashboard. Team licence for up to fifteen developers, renewed annually with this key.

reviews.author: Petra L.
reviews.body: Caught real bugs in week one. CI plugin setup was fiddly.

reviews.author: Amir F.
reviews.body: Dashboard makes triaging findings across repos painless.

products.name: Backend Engineering with Python & FastAPI
products.shortDescription: Build and deploy production APIs with FastAPI.
products.longDescription: A project-based course covering FastAPI fundamentals, SQLAlchemy, Alembic migrations, and deployment to a containerized cloud environment. Includes lifetime access and downloadable source code for every module.

reviews.author: Noor H.
reviews.body: The migrations module alone was worth the price.

reviews.author: Ben C.
reviews.body: Clear pacing, real projects, no filler.

products.name: Vue 3 & TypeScript: From Fundamentals to Production
products.shortDescription: Composition API, TypeScript, and Vite in a single track.
products.longDescription: Covers the Composition API, typed props and emits, Pinia state management, and a full production build pipeline with Vite. Includes quizzes, a capstone project, and a completion certificate.

reviews.author: Elif K.
reviews.body: Great structure; wish there were more on testing.

reviews.author: Diego R.
reviews.body: Finally a course that treats TypeScript as first-class.

products.name: AWS for Backend Engineers: CDK in Practice
products.shortDescription: Infrastructure as code on AWS using the Python CDK.
products.longDescription: Hands-on modules building VPCs, ECS Fargate services, RDS instances, and CI/CD pipelines with AWS CDK in Python. Ends with a capstone deploying a full three-tier application.

reviews.author: Fatima Z.
reviews.body: Took this straight into a real project the same week.

products.name: SQL for Application Developers
products.shortDescription: Practical, index-aware SQL for building real applications.
products.longDescription: Covers query design, indexing strategy, transactions, and common pitfalls when an ORM sits between you and the database. Exercises run against a real Postgres instance provided in the browser sandbox.

reviews.author: Ravi S.
reviews.body: The indexing chapter changed how I write queries.

reviews.author: Claire M.
reviews.body: Best SQL course I've taken, and I've taken a few.

products.name: The Refactoring Field Guide
products.shortDescription: Small, safe changes that leave code better than you found it.
products.longDescription: A catalogue of refactorings organised by the smell that motivates them, each with a worked before-and-after and the test that keeps it honest. DRM-free EPUB and PDF.

reviews.author: Dana R.
reviews.body: The smell-first ordering makes it usable at work.

reviews.author: Tom H.
reviews.body: Wish the examples covered more than one language.

products.name: Distributed Systems for the Impatient
products.shortDescription: Consensus, replication and failure, without the maths degree.
products.longDescription: Explains why distributed systems fail the way they do — partial failure, clock skew, split brain — and what the standard answers actually cost. Diagrams over proofs throughout.

reviews.author: Priya N.
reviews.body: Finally understand quorums. Worth it for that alone.

products.name: Debugging: A Systematic Approach
products.shortDescription: Replace guessing with a method that converges on the cause.
products.longDescription: A repeatable loop — reproduce, bisect, hypothesise, test — applied to memory corruption, race conditions, and the bugs that only appear in production.

reviews.author: Marcus L.
reviews.body: The bisect chapter paid for the book twice over.

reviews.author: Elena V.
reviews.body: Solid, if a little dry in the middle third.

products.name: Designing Data Contracts
products.shortDescription: Schemas that survive the second team that depends on them.
products.longDescription: Versioning, compatibility and deprecation for APIs and event streams, with the migration strategies that let a producer change without breaking consumers it has never met.

reviews.author: Sofia K.
reviews.body: The deprecation playbook is the best part.

products.name: The Pragmatic Code Reviewer
products.shortDescription: Reviews that find defects without starting fights.
products.longDescription: What to look for, what to leave alone, and how to write a comment that gets acted on. Includes checklists for security, concurrency and API changes.

reviews.author: Ben A.
reviews.body: Changed the tone of our whole review culture.

reviews.author: Yuki T.
reviews.body: Short, which is the point.

products.name: Observability from First Principles
products.shortDescription: Logs, metrics and traces, and when each one is the wrong tool.
products.longDescription: Builds up from a single request id to distributed tracing, with a hard look at cardinality, sampling and what an alert should mean before anyone is paged.

reviews.author: Nadia F.
reviews.body: The chapter on alert fatigue should be mandatory.

products.name: Writing for Engineers
products.shortDescription: Design docs, incident reports and commit messages that land.
products.longDescription: Technical writing aimed squarely at engineers: how to open a design doc so it gets read, how to write an incident report that teaches, and why the commit message is documentation.

reviews.author: Chris P.
reviews.body: My design docs get comments now instead of silence.

reviews.author: Amara O.
reviews.body: Read it in a weekend, use it every week.

products.name: QueryLens Profiler
products.shortDescription: Find the slow query before your users do.
products.longDescription: Attaches to Postgres and MySQL, samples live traffic, and ranks statements by total time rather than worst case. Single-developer licence, one year of updates.

reviews.author: Jonas W.
reviews.body: Found an unindexed join costing us 40% of CPU.

products.name: Sentinel Log Viewer
products.shortDescription: Structured log search that runs on your laptop.
products.longDescription: Reads JSON logs from files, stdin or an S3 prefix, indexes them locally, and answers filter queries instantly. No agent, no server, nothing leaves the machine.

reviews.author: Ines G.
reviews.body: Replaced three shell aliases and a lot of grep.

reviews.author: Peter M.
reviews.body: The S3 mode is why I bought it.

products.name: Cascade Diagram Studio
products.shortDescription: Architecture diagrams that stay in version control.
products.longDescription: Text-first diagramming: describe the system, get a rendered diagram, and diff the source like any other file. Exports SVG and PNG at any scale.

reviews.author: Laura B.
reviews.body: Our diagrams are finally reviewable in PRs.

products.name: Payload API Client
products.shortDescription: A REST and GraphQL client that keeps requests in the repo.
products.longDescription: Collections are plain files you commit, so a request that reproduced a bug is still there next month. Environments, secrets from your keychain, and scripted assertions.

reviews.author: Owen D.
reviews.body: Committed collections are such an obvious idea.

reviews.author: Mei L.
reviews.body: Fast, and it doesn't want an account.

products.name: Bastion Secrets Manager
products.shortDescription: Team secrets with an audit trail, self-hosted.
products.longDescription: Encrypted at rest with per-environment keys, access scoped by team, and every read recorded. Runs as a single binary against Postgres. Five-seat licence.

reviews.author: Tariq H.
reviews.body: Audit log satisfied our auditor on the first pass.

products.name: Meridian Load Tester
products.shortDescription: Load profiles that look like your actual traffic.
products.longDescription: Replays production access patterns rather than hammering one endpoint, so the bottleneck it finds is the one you would have hit. Reports p50 through p99.9.

reviews.author: Greta S.
reviews.body: Traffic replay is worth the price on its own.

reviews.author: Hugo C.
reviews.body: Caught a connection-pool limit before launch.

products.name: Atlas Schema Migrator
products.shortDescription: Reversible migrations with a dry run you can trust.
products.longDescription: Plans every migration against a shadow database first and reports locks, rewrites and estimated duration before anything touches production.

reviews.author: Rafael Q.
reviews.body: The lock report stopped a very bad Friday.

products.name: Docker and Compose in Practice
products.shortDescription: Images, layers and Compose files that don't fight you.
products.longDescription: Builds a multi-service application from an empty directory, covering multi-stage builds, layer caching, health checks and the differences that bite in production.

reviews.author: Nils E.
reviews.body: Layer caching finally clicked.

reviews.author: Aisha R.
reviews.body: Good pace, assumes a little Linux.

products.name: Testing Python at Scale
products.shortDescription: Fast suites, honest fixtures, and tests that stay green.
products.longDescription: Pytest beyond the basics: fixture scope, parametrisation, test doubles that don't lie, and keeping a four-thousand-test suite under two minutes.

reviews.author: Lena M.
reviews.body: The section on flaky tests earned its keep.

products.name: System Design Interview Workshop
products.shortDescription: Eight designs, whiteboarded end to end.
products.longDescription: Works through eight systems — a URL shortener to a news feed — with the estimation, the trade-offs and the follow-up questions interviewers actually ask.

reviews.author: Victor A.
reviews.body: Got the offer. The estimation drills did it.

reviews.author: Hana J.
reviews.body: Two designs felt rushed, the rest were excellent.

products.name: Terraform to Production
products.shortDescription: State, modules and the blast radius of a plan.
products.longDescription: Remote state and locking, module boundaries that survive a second environment, and reading a plan for the replacements it is quietly proposing.

reviews.author: Kofi B.
reviews.body: 'Read the plan' should be tattooed on everyone.

products.name: Redis Patterns for Web Apps
products.shortDescription: Caching, sessions, queues — and their failure modes.
products.longDescription: Each pattern paired with what happens when the node is lost: TTLs and eviction policies, cache stampedes, and why a queue on Redis needs more thought than it first appears.

reviews.author: Silvia D.
reviews.body: The eviction-policy lesson saved our carts.

reviews.author: Adam F.
reviews.body: Would like more on Cluster mode.

products.name: Accessible Frontend Engineering
products.shortDescription: WCAG in practice, from semantics to focus management.
products.longDescription: Keyboard navigation, focus traps, live regions and colour contrast, tested with real screen readers rather than an automated score.

reviews.author: Grace W.
reviews.body: Testing with an actual screen reader was eye-opening.
